pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: What Do People Do All Day?
work.note: What Do People Do All Day? é um livro ilustrado de Richard Scarry que mostra o trabalho de cada profissão. A referência é o livro das profissões numa cidade: What do you do?.

pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

facts.label: Situação
facts.sub: In the USA, “What do you do?” is one of the first questions at a party. It means “What is your job?” and people expect a short answer.

facts.big: “What do you do?” asks about your job.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: It is a common small-talk question, not “What are you doing now?”

facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: It connects Brooklyn and Manhattan and opened in 1883.

facts.big: Restaurant servers in the USA usually get tips.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: Tips are a big part of their income, so 15 to 20 percent is normal.

facts.label: Educação e tom
facts.sub: After someone says their job, ask “Do you like it?” It shows interest and keeps the chat friendly.

compare.br: In Brazil, people often ask first about your family, your city or your team (time) before your job.
compare.us: In the USA, people often ask about your job early. It is a way to start a chat, not to judge.
compare.tip: Say your job and add one more detail: “I’m a teacher. I love my students.”

pages.title: A teacher and a cook in Brooklyn · 1/3
paragraphs: Brooklyn is a big part of New York City. Many people live and work there. Two neighbors, Maria and Ava, talk on the stairs. “**What do you do, Maria?**” asks Ava. “**I’m a teacher**,” says Maria. “**And you?**”
“**I’m a cook**,” says Ava. “**I work in a restaurant.**” Maria says, “Cool! **Do you like your job?**” “**Yes, I do. It’s busy but fun**,” Ava says. She works long hours, so she is tired at night.
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: A teacher and a cook in Brooklyn · 2/3
paragraphs: “**Where is the restaurant?**” asks Maria. “**On Fifth Avenue**,” says Ava. “**Come for lunch!**” Maria answers, “**I will!** Thanks.” Ava says, “**See you at lunch!**”

There is a famous book about jobs. In 1968, Richard Scarry made “What Do People Do All Day?” It shows Busytown, where everyone has a job. The farmer grows food, the builder makes houses, and the mechanic fixes cars. In the book, each job helps the town.

pages.title: A teacher and a cook in Brooklyn · 3/3
paragraphs: This is true in real life too. A teacher helps children learn. A cook makes food for hungry people. A driver takes people home. When you ask “What do you do?”, you learn how a person helps their town.
